qs: tell me about the everythingcalendar repo
a: everythingcalendar is a Jerry Zhu repo with a frontend and a backend. The frontend is run with npm (npm i, npm run dev) and the backend is a Python app run with app.py in a virtualenv.

qs: how do i run the everythingcalendar frontend
how to start frontend in everythingcalendar
a: everythingcalendar's frontend is run by cd frontend, setting up a .env file, then npm i and npm run dev.

qs: how do i run the everythingcalendar backend
how to start backend in everythingcalendar
a: everythingcalendar's backend is run by cd backend, setting up a .env file, creating a python3 venv, installing requirements.txt, and running python3 app.py.

qs: what must pass before merging a PR in everythingcalendar
a: everythingcalendar requires linter tests to pass before a PR is merged.

qs: what is on the everythingcalendar todo list
which aws services does everythingcalendar use
a: everythingcalendar's TODO list mentions cloudformation, terraform and kubernetes (EKS); right now only ECS and ECR are used.
everythingcalendar is at https://github.com/Bobliuuu/everythingcalendar.

qs: tell me about the Global-PayChain repo
a: Global-PayChain is a proof-of-concept demo for an application that revolutionizes international money transfers.

qs: what tech stack does Global-PayChain use
a: Global-PayChain was built with the T3 Next.JS stack, with Solidity and a Hardhat clone of the Solana testnet in the backend.

qs: how does Global-PayChain do cross-chain transfers
a: Global-PayChain has Solidity smart contracts with gas optimization, plus cross-chain token transfers using the Squid SDK (Axelar) and the Metamask SDK with Ethers.JS.
Global-PayChain's architecture uses Next.js Auth and decentralized storage, with Prisma storing credentials and JWT tokens.
To run Global-PayChain, cd global-paychain, run npm i and npm run dev, then open localhost port 3000 in a browser.
Global-PayChain also has a hardhat-fork-sol folder, an Alchemy virtual environment to test Solana mainnet transactions without wasting gas fees; run npm i and hardhat test there.
Global-PayChain was validated with unit tests and comprehensive testing in Hardhat and local testing.

qs: what are the limitations of Global-PayChain
a: Known issues in Global-PayChain: Send does not currently work on the Next.JS demo because it needs integration with the Alchemy hardhat VM. Future work is Axelar general message passing cross-chain.
Global-PayChain is at https://github.com/Bobliuuu/Global-PayChain.
